question: When troubleshooting a high-voltage switching power supply (SMPS), why is using a standard, un-isolated oscilloscope probe on the primary side switching transistor extremely dangerous?
choices: A. It connects the primary side "hot" ground directly to the oscilloscope's earth ground, creating a massive short circuit
B. It will erase the oscilloscope's memory
C. The high frequency will shatter the CRT
D. The probe will act as an antenna and cause interference

question: To safely test for an open diode in a circuit using a DMM, what must usually be done?
choices: A. Test it while the circuit is fully powered
B. Lift (desolder) at least one leg of the diode from the PCB to prevent parallel components from providing a false reading
C. Apply a high AC voltage
D. Measure its temperature

question: A worded circuit: A 555 timer is wired in astable mode. The output is stuck HIGH. You measure the voltage on the timing capacitor and find it is 0V. What is the most likely fault?
choices: A. The discharge pin (Pin 7) is shorted
B. The power supply is disconnected
C. The timing capacitor is dead shorted to ground
D. Resistor Ra is open

question: What is the "Shotgun" approach to troubleshooting, and why is it generally discouraged by professional engineers?
choices: A. Using a shotgun to destroy the device
B. Carefully measuring every single voltage before touching a component
C. Using an oscilloscope to view the entire spectrum
D. Blindly replacing components on a board until it starts working, which is expensive, time-consuming, and risks damaging the PCB
